text:
maria: Quick FYI — I ran the longevity holdout (64k tokens) against SmoothMix (SmoothQuant + activation-aware tweaks) vs AWQ and GPTQ on LlamaX-13B. Some weird deltas, posting raw notes.

kevin: Nice, small summary first? :eyes:

sophia: curious on metrics — perplexity? em/rouge?

maria: short summary: FP8 SmoothMix gives best token-level perf (ppl down ~1.7 relative), INT8 AWQ close on ppl but worse EM on QA slices. GPTQ stable but higher latency. However SmoothMix shows KV-cache drift on very long prefixes — hallucination spikes on the 50–64k tail.

tyler: woah, KV drift — can you paste the failure pattern?

maria: snippet from eval harness logs: 
```
PROMPT_LEN=62000
MODEL=llamax-13b-smoothmix-fp8
-> step=145 generated incoherent footer, repeated entity tokens
score.delta.EM = -2.3% abs vs float32
```

kevin: EM drop 2.3% absolute on which dataset?

maria: on the QA holdout (longQA-64k), not on short QA. On summarization (longSum) Rouge-L drop is smaller (~0.9 abs).

sophia: do we know if it's quantization-induced activation scaling mismatch across attention layers?

maria: hypothesis: activation-aware scaling reduces layerwise range early, but when KV cache replays long prefix, scaling mismatch accumulates. The SmoothQuant per-tensor calibration was done on 16k windows; we need 64k-aware calibration.

tyler: Hm. What about mixed configs — FP8 for attn weights + INT8 for MLP? Any tests?

maria: ran a mix: FP8-attn + INT8-mlp (smoothmix hybrid). Ppl ~1.2 better than full INT8, EM drop reduced to 1.1 abs but latency slightly worse than pure FP8 (tail latency +18ms).

kevin: numbers for p50/p95 latency? deployment profile matters.
maria: p50/p95 (batch=1, g4dn-type): FP8 SmoothMix = 120ms / 320ms, Hybrid = 135ms / 360ms, AWQ INT8 = 145ms / 390ms, GPTQ INT8-opt = 160ms / 420ms. Token throughput favors FP8 by ~12%.

sophia: interesting. Did you try calibrating with longer sequences (64k) and re-run?

maria: not yet — queued. I did a small synthetic re-calib (sliding windows up to 32k) and it reduced KV drift but didn't eliminate it. So next step: full 64k calibration and check act-aware clipping heuristics.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary bucket created: eng-ml-quant-canary-02 (3 nodes).

kevin: can we run a canary config: smoothmix-fp8 + 64k-calib + override kv-eviction=aggressive ? Want to measure rollback risk.

maria: will run. command i'm using: `python eval/run_holdout.py --model smoothmix-fp8 --calib-window 65536 --holdout longQA-64k --save=run_2166`

quant-bot: Note: recent kernel change (fused-attn v2) can change activation distribution. Link: https://internal/runbook/kernels/attn_v2

sophia: good catch — that could interact with FP8 numerics. Was the SmoothMix build using fused-attn v1?

maria: yes, run_2165 used attn_v1. Can re-run with v2 to isolate.

tyler: For rollout criteria, proposal: require EM delta <= 0.5 abs vs float on QA holdout AND no >5x increase in hallucination events measured by repetition ratio on last 10% tokens.

kevin: agreed. Also add latency SLO: p95 < 400ms for dedicated tier.

maria: plan: 1) full 64k calibration + run with attn_v1/v2 2) hybrid FP8-attn INT8-mlp ablation 3) run canary on eng-ml-quant-canary-02 and collect traces + kv metrics 4) add an automated detection in eval harness for 'kv drift' based on token-entropy collapse.

sophia: timeline?

maria: starting runs now, estimate 6h for full calib/ablation, then canary deploy tomorrow morning. I'll drop a follow-up with artifacts + perf tables. :rocket:

kevin: thanks — if the canary looks clean, we can stage an A/B on 10% traffic for Dedicated next week.

maria: ack. saving logs to s3://redwood-ml/experiments/2166004321_smoothmix_longholdout/ — will attach eval jsons.

infra-bot: storage-bot: Archive created at s3://redwood-ml/experiments/2166004321_smoothmix_longholdout/metadata.json

tyler: one more ask — capture model slices by prompt type; some prompt templates (code-like) are less affected. That could be important for routing policies.

maria: noted — slicing by template will be in the run.

kevin: great thread. Ping me when canary metrics land. :thumbsup:
